question.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Parametric Curve
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952905/assets/c9371d5e2bb921b4f5e58423bbce492f2b555122ee42bd861040b57d01070353.png)

For the parametric curve (shown above)

$$
x=2(t+1),\,y=4{t}^{2},\,-1\le t<1,
$$

 find the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at the point $P$ on the curve where $t=0.$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=2,\,{y}^{′}(t)=8t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{8t}{2}=4t.
$$

At the point where $t=0$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dy}{dx} & =4(0) \\  & =0\,.\end{aligned}
$$
